commitResults.messageTitle: Prevent failed saves from corrupting data files
commitResults.messageBody:
Saving directly over an existing file can leave it truncated or
partially written if a write fails. This violates the Developer
Guide's requirement to preserve previously saved data.

Write JSON content to a temporary file in the same directory, then
atomically replace the destination after writing completes. Report
a save error if atomic replacement is unsupported, preserving the
existing file.

Apply this protection to all JSON saves. Keep the existing behavior
where in-memory changes remain after a save failure and the three
domain files are saved separately.

Add regression tests for write and replacement failures, and update
the saving documentation to explain the guarantees.

Fixes #157

commitResults.messageBody:
Verify that incomplete temporary files do not affect JSON loading
or later saves, and that successful saves leave no new temp files.

commitResults.messageTitle: Preserve file permissions during atomic saves
commitResults.messageBody:
Atomic replacement can overwrite read-only files and discard their
permissions.

Reject unwritable destinations and copy existing permissions before
replacement. Add regression tests for permission preservation and
failure handling.

commitResults.messageBody:

Skip domain-data saves for help and exit while retaining list as a
save retry. Add regression tests and document the save exceptions.

Strict phone validation rejects useful contact details, and equivalent
Singapore spellings can create separate member identities.

Normalize recognized Singapore inputs and retain other nonblank entries
with a shared nonblocking warning. Apply the same rules to lookup and
storage, and add an explicit phone search for entries containing spaces.

with regression tests. Keep longer entries accessible in the UI.

commitResults.messageTitle: Protect unread member data during startup
commitResults.messageBody:
Normalizing legacy phone entries can reveal duplicate identities.
Starting with an empty list after a load failure risks overwriting the
unread member records when a later command saves the model.

Stop initialization with an actionable recovery message instead of
exposing an empty list. Preserve the original failure cause and file.
Test conflicting normalized entries, unreadable data, legacy contacts
and the missing-file sample-data path.

The phone rules now distinguish recognized Singapore formats from
nonstandard entries that are saved with a warning.

Explain normalization, exact-text duplicate detection, phone-only
searches and the limits of foreign-number handling in the user guide.
Update the developer guide, glossary and manual regression scenarios.
Document recovery from unreadable member files without silently merging
member points or histories.

commitResults.messageTitle: Reject digitless phone input without losing data
commitResults.messageBody:
Nonblank placeholders such as Not available and --- can be registered
as phone identities even though they contain no phone digits.

Require a Unicode decimal digit for newly supplied add/edit phone
values and report a specific validation error. Keep the model and
storage permissive for legacy nonblank notes so users can retrieve and
correct existing records without losing membership data.

Cover rejection without state or file changes and legacy lookup,
editing and persistence. Update the user and developer guides.

commitResults.messageTitle: Warn about possible duplicate phone entries
commitResults.messageBody:
Exact phone equality misses overseas formatting variants and numbers
embedded in annotations or lists.

Compare complete number segments of at least seven digits and warn
about overlaps across all members, including hidden records. Keep this
advisory comparison separate from identity checks so exact duplicates
remain blocked and suspicious entries can still be saved unchanged.

Exclude the edited member and skip overlap checks for edits without a
phone field. Test both input directions, multiple matches, persistence,
false positives and digitless rejection. Document the matching limits.
